context: A tutor and two students plan a campus bicycle-theft mapping project.

lines.text: Now turn to Section Three. You will hear a tutor and two students discussing a campus bicycle-theft project.
Questions twenty-one to twenty-four. Complete the flowchart. Write no more than two words for each answer. First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
Let's lock the mapping sequence before you walk the campus.
First we design the grid — squares on the campus plan, not freehand sketches.
Then we run a walkthrough with security so we don't miss the service yards.
After that we log the stands — every rack, even the broken ones.
And finally we photograph the damage and pin the images to the grid.
Questions twenty-five to twenty-seven. Complete the summary. Write one word only for each answer. First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-five to twenty-seven.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-five to twenty-seven.
What's slowing you down at the moment?
Permissions, honestly. Estates keep postponing the access badges.
We thought about paying porters, but the ethics form only allows a small sticker.
Yes — a five-pound sticker for each bike we tag, not cash.
How are you sending the invitation?
We tried the student app first — wait.
Oh — sorry, actually text. The app notices were ignored.
Questions twenty-eight to thirty. Who will do each task? Choose A or B. The names are on your question paper only. First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-eight to thirty.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-eight to thirty.
Split the remaining jobs so you don't both write the same section.
I'll handle the data tables — I'm faster with the spreadsheet.
lines.note: Paper: A Jade; B Omar. Data tables = Omar.

lines.text: Then I'll write the literature review, since I've already read the police brief.
And the oral presentation to the estates board?
Jade should lead that — she's clearer in meetings.
That's fine — I'll present.
Good. Send me the grid by Friday.
That is the end of Section Three. Now turn to Section Four.
